key_insight: Knowing whether a robot completes a task is not enough to understand its controller. AgentRoboCritic analyzes individual actions to examine how frontier AI agents succeed or fail when directly controlling robots.
problem_solved: Episode-level success rates hide the behaviors and mistakes behind task outcomes, limiting insight into agents that control robots through low-level numerical actions rather than high-level commands.
method: Study frontier multimodal agents performing direct robot control through low-level numerical actions.
Analyze behavior at the action level across 12 manipulation benchmarks.
Introduce AgentRoboCritic for systematic analysis; its implementation and detailed findings are not available in the truncated abstract.
impact: Action-level evaluation could help practitioners diagnose control failures and guide improvements beyond aggregate success rates. The provided excerpt does not establish specific performance gains.
visual_elements: Control-loop diagram: visual observation → multimodal agent → numerical action → robot.
Side-by-side comparison of episode-level pass/fail scoring and action-level analysis.
Action timeline highlighting steps associated with successful behavior or failure.
paper_title: AgentRoboCritic: Understanding the Capability of Frontier Agents on Direct Robot Control
paper_authors: Yiyang Du, Yuxuan Kuang, Qitao Zhao, Yixuan Wang, Zhanqiu Guo
